facts.text: Kommetjie, Afrikaans for "small basin", sits midway down Cape Peninsula’s west coast, overlooking Atlantic swells.
The Slangkop Lighthouse, 33 metres tall, has stood on Kommetjie’s beach since 1919, guiding ships through rocky reefs.
In 1902, businessmen founded Kommetjie as a residential suburb of Cape Town, later modernised with electricity in the 1960s.
Kommetjie’s streets honour early settlers: De Villiers, van der Horst, Seeliger, Benning, Van der Poll, and Kirsten.
Surfers flock to Kommetjie because Atlantic waves rise over hard sandstone reefs, creating ideal conditions for surfing and crayfishing.
The town hosts a vibrant arts scene, with local artists, musicians, writers, and makers shaping Kommetjie’s cultural identity.
